title: The 17-Cent Credit Check: Who Signs the AI Number?
subtitle: In mid-September 2026 OpenAI CFO Sarah Friar told CNBC that agentic credit checks cut unit cost from about $200 to 17 cents. Deloitte found 60% of finance leaders expect AI costs and complexity to rise through 2027. Workiva's Amplify conference heard that 84% of respondents were at least somewhat confident putting unchecked AI numbers into an annual report. A composite Indian mid-cap CFO must decide what the board will sign.
category: AI Cost, Internal Control & CFO Judgment
description: HBS-style teaching case dated 20 September 2026. Public facts: Sarah Friar on CNBC Mad Money (reported 16 September 2026) said OpenAI finance used its own products to cut credit-check cost from about $200 to 17 cents on a run-rate of 2,800 checks the prior year, calling many displaced tasks mundane. Deloitte (CFO Dive, 15 September 2026; 1,434 finance leaders at firms with at least $1 billion revenue, 26 countries) reported 60% expect AI costs and technical complexity to rise substantially through 2027; 54% lead enterprise AI and technology capital allocation; 48% oversee AI and technology spending. Workiva Amplify, Las Vegas, 14 September 2026: CFO Barbara Larson said finance is pulled into strategy and tech decisions before they are made; survey cited by Penny Ashley-Lawrence: 84% at least somewhat confident AI-generated numbers could land in annual reports without a human check. Composite firm: Kalinga Precision Components Ltd. Composite CFO: Nandini Rao.
thumbnail: CREDIT CHECKS FELL FROM $200 TO 17 CENTS. 84% WOULD PUT AN UNCHECKED AI NUMBER IN THE ANNUAL REPORT. WHO SIGNS?
sources: Katherine Li, Business Insider, 16 September 2026, reporting Sarah Friar on CNBC Mad Money: credit checks 2,800/year prior year; cost from $200 to about 17 cents.

CFO Dive, 15 September 2026, Deloitte survey of 1,434 finance leaders: 60% expect AI costs and complexity to rise through 2027; 54% lead AI capital allocation; 48% oversee AI spend. Quote from Ed Hardy, Deloitte.
Denise Lugo, Thomson Reuters Checkpoint News, 18 September 2026: Workiva Amplify 14 September 2026; Barbara Larson; 84% confidence statistic cited by Penny Ashley-Lawrence.
Constellation Research, 9 September 2026 summary of Deloitte Finance Trends 2027 (agentic autonomy 14% fully autonomous on critical decisions; 55% require human oversight).
